reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it depicts a government-associated broadcast of a religious ground-breaking ceremony in Ayodhya, including Narendra Modi's attendance and participation. The decorated religious setting, clergy, attendees, ceremonial object, and speech at a lectern are consistent with that purpose, while the request to subscribe is ordinary channel engagement not linked to money, investment participation, data submission, or a deceptive benefit.

citations.quote: PM Narendra Modi Attends Bhoomi Pujan Ceremony of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi in Ayodhya | Ram temple
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will perform the ground worship
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed the Bhumi Pujan for the reconstruction of Shirram Janmabhoomi Birth Place

opening.argument: The description does more than identify the broadcast: it asks viewers to subscribe and press the bell, then directs them to an external official website and several social accounts. That creates a concrete viewer-action pathway, even though the supplied material does not show a promised payment or reward. The combination leaves open whether the engagement request is intended to funnel viewers toward an external claim or participation flow rather than merely report the ceremony.

citations.quote: Subscribe to #PIB India for official videos on Government of India
All you need to is to press the BELL ICON :bellhop bell: next to the subscribe button
Official website - http://www.pib.nic.in/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ceremonial imagery and title establish the setting, but they do not resolve the separate solicitation in the description. The request to subscribe, activate notifications, and visit an external website remains a real action sequence. Calling it ordinary engagement assumes that no downstream benefit or funnel exists; the supplied evidence does not independently establish that assumption.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The action request is only for channel engagement and updates: the description says to subscribe and press the bell, but it never promises money, an asset, a giveaway, or a withdrawal. The website and social links are identified as official information channels, so the argument supplies no reward-action relationship required for this scam category.

opening.argument: Several distribution signals appear together: a request to subscribe, an instruction to activate the bell, and links to a website plus Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram. The description also uses an urgency-adjacent invitation to stay tuned for the latest updates. These signals can encourage low-effort repeated engagement and movement to external channels, so the possibility of a low-barrier solicitation is not ruled out even though no explicit cash return is shown.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference emphasizes the event's religious content, but that does not negate the promotional distribution pattern attached to the video. A ceremony can be used as attention-grabbing context while the description directs viewers to subscribe, enable notifications, and follow external accounts. The absence of a visible payment request is relevant, but it does not turn every external engagement pathway into ordinary reporting.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The listed signals are routine channel-distribution features, not scam indicators by themselves. Nothing supplied mentions a return, reward, account verification, payment, wallet, or claim process. The description instead frames the links as government updates, while the video title and transcript identify the ceremony, leaving the alleged solicitation unsupported.

opening.argument: Although presented as a ceremony broadcast, the surrounding metadata also functions as promotion for a channel and its connected platforms. It explicitly tells viewers to subscribe, activate the bell, and follow multiple accounts, while promising the latest updates. That makes the content capable of steering viewers into low-barrier participation rather than serving only as neutral coverage; the religious and governmental framing does not itself prove that the engagement pathway is harmless.

Those calls to action are promotional behavior attached to the broadcast. The fact that the setting contains clergy and a public speech does not exclude a separate engagement objective in the description.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a public channel is not promotion of a scam. The supplied call to action requests subscriptions and notifications, not money or a purchase, and the description says the channel provides government videos and updates. The ceremonial frames and transcript support the stated broadcast role, while no evidence shows a deceptive benefit or participation scheme.
